newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Norwegians still against EU, new PM says.
newsitem.headline: Norwegians still against EU, new PM says.

text.p: Norway's new prime minister, Thorbjoern Jagland, said on Wednesday his government would not consider membership of the European Union again any time soon, saying a majority of Norwegians continued to oppose it.

Jagland, on his first visit to Brussels since succeeding veteran premier Gro Harlem Brundtland last October, was asked whether the Norwegian people, who rejected membership in a 1994 referendum, still had the same attitude towards the EU.
"Yes, I'm sorry to say that there is still a rather strong majority against membership," Jagland told a news conference.
He met NATO Secretary-General Javier Solana and European Commissioners Ritt Bjerregaard and Erkki Liikanen during his one-day visit. Norway is a member of the North Atlantic Treaty Organisation.
Jagland, who is pro-EU, said no parties in the Norwegian parliament planned to raise the EU membership discussion in the next parliamentary period.

He indicated that he did not believe the issue would be discussed again before the 15-nation EU has enlarged to take in new members from central and eastern Europe. "And I don't know whether it will be easier to take up the issue after enlargement either," he said.
He said Norway favoured expansion of NATO, and that the country could play an important role in bringing Russia closer to western Europe, partly through the cooperation in the Barents Sea region.
Jagland said his impression was that Solana had had a "pragmatic discussion" this week with Russian Foreign Minister Yevgeny Primakov in Moscow.
